newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA'S WOODIES WIN EIGHTH MAJOR TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA'S WOODIES WIN EIGHTH MAJOR TITLE.

text.p: Local heroes Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge won their eighth Grand Slam doubles title at the Australian Open on Saturday, beating Sebastien Lareau of Canada and American Alex O'Brien in four sets.
The top-seeded Australian pair won their second title in Melbourne, coming from behind to defeat their seventh-seeded rivals 4-6 7-5 7-5 6-3 in just under three hours.
Woodforde and Woodbridge have won the past four Wimbledon titles and took the 1995 and 1996 U.S. Open crowns as well as last year's Olympic title in Atlanta.
The Australian pair, who have 42 career doubles titles, are the fourth most successful men's combination in the Open era.

Americans Peter Fleming and John McEnroe head the list of most successful pairings, winning 57 titles, followed by South Africans Bob Hewitt and Frew McMillan and Spaniards Sergio Casal and Emilio Sanchez.
On Saturday, Woodforde and Woodbridge were named members of the Order of Australia, one of the country's highest honours, in recognition of their Olympic win and their contribution to tennis.
Woodbridge said the win was a useful morale booster before Australia's first-round Davis Cup tie against defending champions France in Sydney next month.
"Going into a match like that with a win like this was great for our confidence," he said.
